name: ALBANIA

flag.title: Flag of Albania
flag.note: Red field with black double-headed eagle

lead: Albania is a small country on the Adriatic Sea, squeezed between mountains and turquoise water. In Albanian, its name Shqipëria means Land of the Eagles. A black two-headed eagle flies on its red flag. Ancient castles, Ottoman bazaars, and hidden beaches fill the land.
geo: Mountains and hills cover almost all of Albania. The northern Albanian Alps are so rugged that villages stayed cut off for centuries. Three big lakes, Shkodër, Ohrid, and Prespa, lie along the borders.
The coast stretches 476 km along the Adriatic and Ionian Seas. The Vjosë River flows free without a single dam. In 2023 it became Europe's first Wild River National Park.
animals: The golden eagle is Albania's national animal. Brown bears roam the northern highlands. Wolves and lynx hide in beech forests. Prespa Lakes have Europe's largest Dalmatian pelican colony.
Loggerhead sea turtles nest on the Ionian coast. Ohrid trout live only in Lake Ohrid and are protected. Flamingos visit Narta Lagoon each winter.
culture: Albanians live by an old honour code called Besa. Your word is your bond. In iso-polyphony, voices weave haunting harmonies. UNESCO lists this music as heritage.
A mayor had grey communist blocks in Tirana painted with bright murals. People eat byrek (flaky cheese pastry) and tavë kosi (baked lamb with yoghurt).
history: Illyrians built hilltop forts here 2,500 years ago. The Ottomans ruled for nearly 500 years from 1479. Hero Skanderbeg held off their army for 25 years.
Independence came in 1912. Dictator Enver Hoxha sealed Albania off from the world and built 173,000 bunkers. Many are now cafés and museums. Albania joined NATO in 2009.
wows: No country has more bunkers per km² than Albania.
In Albania, nodding means no and shaking your head means yes.
Only Albanians call their country Shqipëria.
UNESCO city Gjirokastër has roofs of flat stone slabs, not clay tiles.
Lake Ohrid is over 1.3 million years old, one of the oldest lakes.
Albania ended World War II with more Jews than it started with.
A 600-year-old law code, the Kanun, still guides some Alpine villages.

myths.myth: Albania is in the European Union
myths.fact: Albania is a candidate, not a member. It has been one since 2014.

myths.myth: Mother Teresa was born in India
myths.fact: She was born in Skopje to an Albanian family. Tirana's airport carries her name.
